analysis.one_liner: Adani Energy Solutions builds and operates power transmission lines and electricity distribution networks (including Mumbai's power supply), and is now scaling smart electricity meters and power supply to data centres.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to Sept 2026) were announced on 22 Oct 2026: revenue up 51% YoY, EBITDA up 67%, and profit up 145% YoY to Rs1,364 crore. Despite that, the stock fell roughly 6% on results day itself, apparently on concerns about how quickly the company's large project order book will actually convert into revenue. Separately, in September 2026 Adani Energy Solutions was among several Adani group firms that settled a SEBI case over alleged minimum-public-shareholding lapses for about Rs1.5 crore, without admitting or denying the findings.
analysis.plain_terms: The headline numbers look strong - profit has more than doubled for two straight quarters - and the company has a huge pipeline of transmission and smart-metering projects to build out over the next few years. But the stock itself is still about 70% below its September 2022 peak, and the market's reaction to this quarter's good results was to sell the stock anyway. That gap - strong reported growth, weak price reaction - is the thing to sit with: it suggests the market is more worried about execution, debt, or valuation than about demand for the business.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): revenue from operations Rs9,711 crore (+42% YoY), profit Rs1,237 crore (+129% YoY). Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sept 2026): operational revenue Rs7,167 crore (+51% YoY), EBITDA Rs3,548 crore (+67%), profit Rs1,364 crore (+145% YoY, +10% QoQ). One business-press report flagged that part of the profit jump came from regulatory and tax-related adjustments rather than pure operating performance, though no specific rupee figure was labelled 'non-comparable' - treat the 145% YoY profit growth as somewhat flattered rather than entirely clean. By segment: transmission EBITDA grew a steadier 15%, distribution (Mumbai) EBITDA grew 23% on flat revenue (margin-led), smart metering EBITDA roughly doubled-plus on rapid rollout, and a new 'Energy Solutions' segment (data centres, commercial & industrial supply) contributed meaningfully for the first time.
analysis.performance_read: The stock peaked near Rs4,105 in September 2022 and last closed at Rs1,220 - a 70% drawdown. This company itself was created via a 2015 demerger out of Adani Enterprises (shareholders got 1 transmission share per Adani Enterprises share held), but no demerger or spin-off has happened since listing, so this drawdown is not a corporate-action artifact - it is a straightforward price decline from what in hindsight looks like a stretched 2022 valuation. The picture is mixed by time horizon: over 1 year the stock is up 28% versus Nifty down 13% and peer Power Grid down 12% - a strong recent run. Over 3 years it is up 70%, again ahead of both. But over 5 years it is down 35%, while the Nifty is up 25% and Power Grid is up a much larger 119% - the stock has badly lagged its own sector peer over the longer run, and has still not recovered the 2022 highs.
analysis.valuation_read: Different data sources currently disagree sharply on this stock's valuation - one shows a trailing P/E near 355x and ROE of under 3%, another shows a P/E near 57x and ROE near 9%, with even the underlying share price differing between pulls. This is too large a gap to be rounding; it likely reflects different calculation windows or standalone-vs-consolidated figures. Not verified - check current P/E, P/B and ROE on Screener before concluding whether this is cheap or expensive. What can be said directionally: profit has been growing very fast off a small base (up 145% YoY), which mechanically depresses P/E over time if the price doesn't move - so a very high trailing P/E today may simply reflect that recent growth hasn't fully flowed into trailing-twelve-month earnings yet, rather than the market pricing in no growth at all.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is real but not uniform. Transmission revenue grew a moderate 15-17%, largely volume-led as new lines from a roughly Rs87,000 crore order book come online. Distribution (Mumbai) revenue was nearly flat (+2%) while its EBITDA rose 23% - that segment's improvement is margin-led, not volume-led, and is less durable on its own. Smart metering is the standout: both installs (14.8 million meters) and margins are rising together, backed by a 24.6-million-meter order book worth roughly Rs29,500 crore - this is genuine volume-led growth. The new Energy Solutions segment (data centres, C&I supply) is an emerging growth lever management is pointing to for FY31, but it is too early to size its durability.
analysis.health_read: Net debt stood at roughly Rs41,067 crore, with net debt/EBITDA improving from 4.4x to 3.63x - still a meaningfully leveraged balance sheet typical of a capital-intensive transmission business. Management has guided to Rs20,000-25,000 crore of annual capex going forward, funded partly through a QIP raise (reported variously as up to Rs10,000 crore or a completed Rs3,500 crore tranche - not reconciled) and further borrowing. Credit ratings (CRISIL and India Ratings, both AA+) have held steady despite this, which is a reasonable external check on near-term solvency. The bigger question here is less 'does profit turn into cash' (not independently verified this cycle) and more whether financial risk - leverage funding an aggressive capex programme - outpaces the business risk of executing the order book on time.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters held 73.39% as of end-September 2026, with pledging reported at 0% (not independently verified against a primary filing - check on BSE/Screener before relying on this). On the institutional side, two marquee names have been reducing exposure through 2026: Qatar Investment Authority sold a 0.4% stake in May 2026, and GQG Partners - the US investor well known for backing Adani group stocks after the 2023 Hindenburg episode - cut its holding from 4.14% in June 2026 to somewhere between 1.7% and 3.5% by September (sources disagree on the exact figure). Domestic mutual funds, including SBI MF and Birla MF, have been buyers over the same period, partly absorbing what the foreign investors sold.
strengths: Profit nearly tripled YoY for two consecutive quarters (Q1 FY27 +129%, Q2 FY27 +145%), with EBITDA up 67% in Q2
Transmission order book of roughly Rs87,000 crore across 15 under-construction projects gives multi-year revenue visibility
Smart metering has scaled to 14.8 million installed meters with a 24.6-million-meter, Rs29,500 crore order book still to execute
Credit ratings held at AA+ by both CRISIL and India Ratings through mid-2026 despite the heavy capex programme
watchpoints: Stock fell about 6% on the day Q2 FY27 results were announced, suggesting the market doubts how fast the order book converts to revenue
Net debt of roughly Rs41,000 crore against a guided Rs20,000-25,000 crore annual capex plan - leverage is the key risk to monitor, not demand
Two well-known institutional holders, QIA and GQG Partners, have both been net sellers of the stock through 2026
Reported valuation multiples conflict sharply between data sources (P/E cited as both ~57x and ~355x) - verify independently before drawing conclusions on cheapness
analysis.one_thing: Whether the roughly Rs87,000 crore transmission order book and 24.6-million-meter smart-metering pipeline actually convert into billed revenue and cash on the schedule management has guided - that determines if the last two quarters' profit surge is a durable trend or a near-term peak.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 and Q2 FY27 revenue, EBITDA and profit figures were cross-checked across the company's own newsroom release and three independent business-press reports and are consistent. Shareholding percentages (promoter 73.39%, DII 13.61%, FII ~9.56%, public ~3.44%, as of 30 Sept 2026) were corroborated across multiple independent sources. Not verified: exact current P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE and debt/equity (two source sets disagree sharply - one shows P/E ~355x and ROE ~2.8%, another shows P/E ~57x and ROE ~9.4% - recheck on Screener before publishing a specific figure); exact promoter pledge percentage (reported as 0% but not confirmed against a primary BSE filing); final size and price of the 2026 QIP (reported as both a Rs10,000 crore approval and a completed Rs3,500 crore tranche); the next results date (an unconfirmed analyst estimate of mid-January 2027).
